A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable text, equations, figures and Appendices A–E. The shorter v3 removes the NeurIPS checklist; this is an identifiable deletion, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–E report original transformer-training experiments on generated Boyan-chain tasks, comparisons with batch TD, and numerical verification of theoretical constructions.

after.justification: v3 retains the original training experiments, batch-TD comparisons and numerical verification in Section 4 and Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, transformer architectures, attention masks and constructions implementing TD(0), residual gradient, TD with eligibility traces and average-reward TD are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same generated Boyan-chain policy-evaluation tasks, including representable and non-representable value-function settings. Appendices B–D retain the same task and scenario coverage.

E2.justification: The learned-transformer comparisons against batch TD in Figures 4, 5 and 7 are unchanged. Newly cited related works are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 retains the same settings, including 10 states, feature dimension 4, context length 30, discount 0.9 and 4000 training tasks. Layer configurations, larger-scale settings, optimization and evaluation metrics also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The layer-count analyses, shared versus separate layer parameters, softmax-attention experiments, representability comparison and numerical proof checks are retained without changes in Appendices C–E.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 30 seeds and shaded standard errors in the experimental figures. Removing the checklist's statistical-reporting summary does not remove the corresponding captions or run-count disclosures.

E6.justification: The empirical plots in Figures 1 and 3–8 are visually identical, and their reported findings are unchanged. This includes parameter convergence, similarity to batch TD and numerical agreement of the theoretical constructions.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theorems, corollaries and Appendix A proofs retain the same mathematics. The change from 'blockwise' to 'block-wise' in Appendix A.2 is purely editorial.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: constructive implementation of TD methods, empirical emergence after multi-task TD training, and invariant-set analysis explaining that emergence.

C2.justification: The interpretations and substantive limitations remain: policy evaluation rather than control, limited empirical scale, single-layer theoretical analysis and unresolved convergence guarantees. The conclusion continues onto page 10 in v3; its qualifications are not deleted.

D1.justification: Deleting checklist items 4–5 and 13 removes explicit promises of fully reproducing code upon acceptance and accompanying documentation. Appendix C.1 retains implementation details, hardware, runtime and the promise of public code upon publication. This is a disclosure change, not evidence of changed actual availability.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds eight cited works, including Hochreiter et al. (2001), Müller et al. (2022) and Park et al. (2024). It acknowledges earlier input-based meta-learning and concurrent regret-based transformer training while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 corrects isolated wording errors, including 'in-content' and 'wieght', modestly expands related work and removes the submission checklist. The main narrative and Appendix A–E organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The Section 6 trajectory illustration relabels 'prompt' as 'context'; added references reflow the conclusion and bibliography, and checklist pages disappear. Figures 1–8 and the algorithm displays retain their layout and visual content.

improvement.justification: Section 6 provides more complete attribution, particularly for earlier meta-learning and concurrent regret-based training, and small terminology corrections improve clarity. Scientific evidence and proofs are unchanged. Checklist removal loses some code-release commitments, but Appendix C.1 preserves the practical reproduction details and public-release promise, leaving a limited net improvement.
